# The Model {#sec-model}

The model is kept deliberately small: two definitions per axis, each
with its credited home stated inline, and nothing else. Every object
below is mechanized in Lean 4, and the declaration name is given so a
reader can go straight to it; nothing here depends on Lean syntax to be
read.

## Records, contexts, and claims

A **record** is a finite, append-only sequence of entries,
$\Record := \mathrm{List}\ \mathit{Entry}$, ordered by the prefix
relation $\sqsubseteq$: $w \sqsubseteq w'$ iff $w$ is a prefix of $w'$.
Records grow only by appending — nothing already committed is ever
edited or removed. A **context** $\Context$ stands for everything a
verifier does *not* see: causal history, wall-clock time, key custody,
the existence of other records. A **world** pairs the two,
$\World := \Record \times \Context$.

A **claim** is a predicate over a world,
$\Claim : \Record \to \Context \to \mathrm{Prop}$ — "the entry at
position $k$ was authored by principal $A$," "record $w$ is the
canonical log's current head." The claim, not the record alone, is what
a verifier is asked to check.

**The declared axiom base.** $\mathit{Entry}$ and $\Context$ are
introduced as opaque types (`Entry`, `Context`), which is what keeps
every result below parametric: no theorem may inspect an entry's
structure or a context's. Two genuine assumptions accompany them —
`Context.inhabited`, that some context exists, and `Context.nontrivial`,
that two distinct ones do. Those four declarations are everything this
development adds to Lean's own `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`.

`Context.nontrivial` is consumed at three sites, and all three are
non-vacuity witnesses: that undetermined claims exist at all
(`exists_undetermined_claim`), and the two undetermined rows of
@sec-cell-table (`exists_undetermined_monotone`,
`authoredAbsentClaim_not_determined`). Over a one-element context every
claim is trivially determined, so without it the determination axis
would be vacuous and those rows empty.

**What a checker must trust.** Nothing mathematical is assumed. The four
declarations above are modeling opacity, not asserted theorems, and no
result rests on an unproved mathematical fact: where this paper leans on
Rice and Rice–Shapiro it cites them, and neither is axiomatized, so no
Lean proof appeals to either. The dependency on a
mathematics library is confined to a single import in a single file,
which brings in a computability development for the computable stratum.
The core, the verification ceiling, the transport law and both instances
are library-free; what is not is the computable stratum's own content,
including the certifiability half of @sec-cell-table's first row.

## The offline verifier

A **commitment** $\Gamma$ (`Commitment`) fixes a type $\Comm$ of
committed values, a function $C : \Record \to \Comm$ producing one, a
binding axiom on $C$, and a relation $VC$ certifying that the record
behind one committed value extends the record behind another.

**Binding here is exact, and that is a real limitation.** The axiom is
injectivity of $C$, which no compressing function satisfies; the
development states the consequence outright, that binding with
compression is unsatisfiable, and every commitment it instantiates is
the identity. So the mechanized commitment is an information-theoretic
idealization of a digest rather than a digest. What a hash function
supplies instead is *computational* binding, and the distance between
the two is exactly the binding residual of @sec-floor — granted, not
proved.

A **scheme** for $\Claim$ under $\Gamma$ (`Scheme`) is a certificate
type $\mathit{Proof}$ together with a verifier
$V : \Comm \to \mathit{Proof} \to \mathrm{Prop}$ that decides, from a
committed value and a certificate alone — never from the record or the
context — whether $\Claim$ holds. This is the paper's one modeling
commitment: **the verifier's type is the offline property**. The
constraint is on what $V$ may consult, not on how large a certificate
may be; size bounds belong to the polynomial stratum, which this
development does not mechanize.

Completeness is stated as certificate *existence*, never as a bundled
prover, and that is forced rather than stylistic: a scheme carrying an
efficient prover would, composed with an efficient $C$ and $V$, decide
$\phihat$ outright — so a characterization claiming a scheme for every
determined, certifiable claim would carry an unconditional
$\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$ obligation. Bare witness existence is what
keeps @sec-theorem free of it.

Two verifiers of the same commitment can disagree about how much they
trust what they see. The model distinguishes exactly two soundness
flavors, both over the same scheme machinery:

- **Snapshot-sound** (`SnapshotSound`): the certificate is valid for the
  record as it stood when the certificate was produced. Nothing is
  claimed about what happens as the record grows.
- **Enduring-sound** (`EnduringSound`): the certificate remains valid
  for every extension of the record. A certificate produced today keeps
  verifying against tomorrow's, larger record.

The distinction is not cosmetic. It is what lets a single classical
notion — "observable property," bundling semi-decidability with
stability — pull apart into two independent axes in this setting
(@sec-factorization).

A scheme's certificate and verifier are graded by the computational
power required to run them. Three strata, in decreasing generality:

- $\oracle$ — no computability constraint; the verifier may decide
  anything. Certifiability here is `NPMembership`, an idealized
  existence-of-a-checker condition carrying no complexity bound, and
  every record predicate satisfies it (@sec-theorem).
- $\computable$ — the verifier's components are computable over a
  `Primcodable` alphabet, and certifiability is `ComputableMembership`,
  which does bind: it demands a `ComputablePred` checker.
- $\polynomial$ — the verifier runs in polynomial time on a
  polynomially-sized certificate. This stratum is *described here and
  not mechanized*: no predicate in the development encodes those bounds,
  which is part of why its theorems are stated as conjectures
  (@sec-theorem).

A fourth, intermediate stratum — requiring only classical decidability
of the commitment's equality test — adds no content: classical
decidability is universal by $\texttt{Classical.propDecidable}$, so its
verdicts coincide with the oracle stratum's. It survives in the
mechanization as constructive scaffolding that de-risked the computable
stratum, credited honestly rather than presented as a fourth grade. The
tower used throughout is $\oracle \supset \computable \supset
\polynomial$; the polynomial stratum's theorems remain open
(@sec-theorem).

## The three axes

Three independent conditions on a claim $\Claim$, each defined once,
without reference to any scheme:

**Determination** (`Determined`).
$\Det(\Claim) := \forall\, w\; \xi\; \xi',\ \Claim\ w\ \xi \leftrightarrow \Claim\ w\ \xi'$
— the claim's truth value does not depend on the context, only on the
record. Equivalently, $\Claim$ factors through the projection that
forgets context: $\Det(\Claim) \leftrightarrow \exists\, \psi,\ \Claim =
(\lambda\, w\; \_.\ \psi\ w)$, membership in the image of the pullback
$\pstar$ along that projection (`determined_iff_factors`). Where
$\Det(\Claim)$ holds, write $\phihat$ for the resulting record-only
predicate (`determinedProj`).

**Certifiability** (at stratum $Q$). Whether $\phihat$ is
semi-decidable at $Q$'s power — $\Sigma_1$ at the computable stratum
and, at the polynomial one, $\mathrm{NP}$ with genuine size and time
bounds, in the intended-but-unmechanized sense just noted.
The axis is defined on $\phihat$ rather than on $\Claim$, so it exists
only where determination holds; @sec-cell-table turns on that
dependency.

**Monotonicity** (`Monotone`).
$\Mono(\Claim) := \forall\, w\; w'\; \xi,\ \Claim\ w\ \xi \to w \sqsubseteq w' \to \Claim\ w'\ \xi$
— once true, a claim stays true as the record is extended. For
determined $\Claim$ this is equivalent to $\phihat$ being upward-closed
(`UpClosed`, `monotone_iff_projUpClosed`): $\UpC(\psi) := \forall\, w\;
w',\ w \sqsubseteq w' \to \psi\ w \to \psi\ w'$.

These three conditions are the paper's entire vocabulary. Everything
that follows is a statement about how they combine.
